metaDescription: German Shepherd vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so German Shepherd boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Plan German Shepherd social milestones around the schedule rows, not the other way around, because the 16-week finish is the usual green light clinics cite for broader German Shepherd exposure.
Weight range 50-90 lb (23-41 kg) and grooming needs (Heavy double coat; brush several times weekly.) belong in the same German Shepherd household ops list as vaccine dates when busy weeks collide.
If your German Shepherd is also monitored for elbow dysplasia, ask whether bloodwork or orthopedic checks can share a visit with a booster to cut missed German Shepherd appointments.
After the German Shepherd puppy/kitten series, keep adult DA2PP / DHPP and rabies renewals on 7/3/1-day reminders so year-two surprises disappear.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Delayed German Shepherd boosters usually need one well-timed catch-up, not a homemade double dose, because spacing rules protect the puppy and guilt math does not.
Bring prior dates for every German Shepherd row (8, 12, 16, 16 weeks on this page’s plan) so clinics can decide whether an extra DA2PP / DHPP booster is required based on gap length and age.
If rabies was the missed German Shepherd item, legal and boarding consequences stack on top of medical ones — restore compliance before the next German Shepherd kennel reservation.
PetClues should hold both the new German Shepherd due date and the certificate photo so household members stop arguing about which fridge sticky note is current.

faqs.question: When does the German Shepherd core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my German Shepherd misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read German Shepherd health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the German Shepherd adult health guide for breed predispositions such as hip dysplasia, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
